conditional_supplier_grounding.definition_hypotheses: Probability space, sub-sigma-algebra G, integrable X, G-measurable integrable version Y satisfying equal integrals on each G-event. No completeness or finite-atom condition imposed by definition.
conditional_supplier_grounding.hedge_general_algorithm: General measurable random loss vectors need not make history finite. Conditional categorical law is a supplied sampler contract; indicators and history-measurable x_ti are bounded/integrable. No new current-loss predictability, independence, adversary restriction, sampler construction or regret guarantee is introduced.
conditional_supplier_grounding.fixed_loss_marginals: For deterministic x_t, apply the defining identity to event Omega to deduce the old marginal law. Fixed loss sequence ensures weights and x_t are deterministic despite earlier action draws.
conditional_supplier_grounding.bandit_consumer_integrability: Fixed or deterministic history-dependent reward rules with finite arms and horizon give finite action-history tree. Values are finite on each atom, so all estimates and required squares have finite range and are integrable; atom calculations characterize conditional expectation.
conditional_supplier_grounding.exp4_support_boundary: For a supported coordinate, the local atom calculation requires only its probability positive. Unsupported coordinates have zero advice from every expert because Q>0; no false componentwise unbiasedness is claimed there. Its potential proof is pathwise, not bounded-loss Hedge regret.
